claims.text: Traditional EAM references insufficiently represent the many atomic configurations of an ab initio multicomponent-alloy liquid.
Replacing EAM references with MLIPs will better capture the configurational diversity of multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
The proposed improvement applies to both solid and liquid configurations.
High-entropy alloys near their melting points have a large number of distinct atomic environments.
An MLIP trained on ab initio configurations can serve as the reference potential in thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method is applicable near the melting temperatures of alloys containing at least five elements.
An MLIP provides a smoother potential-energy landscape than an EAM reference.
An MLIP provides a potential-energy landscape that is more representative of ab initio liquid configurations than an EAM potential.
MLIPs have sufficiently flexible functional forms and data-driven parameterizations to represent a wider variety of atomic configurations than EAM references.
Greater configurational expressiveness improves phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target states.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap lowers the variance of free-energy estimates along the integration path.
MLIP references will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The expected benefit depends on the MLIP being trained on relevant solid and liquid atomic configurations.
The proposed benefit may fail when relevant liquid phenomena are absent from the MLIP training data.
The proposed benefit may fail for alloy compositions far outside the MLIP training domain.
